cases.exposure_context_quote: Here, we report a rare case of paraquat poisoning in an individual using cannabis, adhering to the CARE 2020 Guidelines.
cases.agent_quote: Four days ago, he had consumed 10–15 mL of a 24% (w/V; paraquat dichloride 24% SL) paraquat solution.
cases.circumstance: accidental ingestion under the influence of marijuana; discloses exposure to guardians on third post-ingestion day who transported him to a nearby healthcare facility

symptoms.finding: vomiting with hematemesis and regurgitated food particles
symptoms.quote: The day after ingestion, he experienced multiple episodes of vomiting, characterized by the presence of blood and food particles.
He also reported complaints of heartburn, difficulty swallowing and reduced urine production.
He also reported complaints of heartburn, difficulty swallowing and reduced urine production.

symptoms.finding: intraoral mucosal erosion with haemorrhagic manifestations
symptoms.quote: However, notable intraoral mucosal erosion accompanied by haemorrhagic manifestations was observed (Figure 1).

symptoms.finding: respiratory deterioration with falling oxygen saturation
symptoms.quote: On evaluation, during the third day of ICU admission, a gradual decrement in oxygen saturation levels and a reduction in urine output was seen.

cases.time_to_care: presented on the third post-ingestion day (ingestion 4 days before ER arrival)

labs.name: PaO2/FiO2 ratio
labs.quote: Arterial blood gas (ABG) analysis demonstrated a deteriorated PaO2/FiO2 ratio, measuring below 100, indicative of compromised oxygen exchange.

labs.name: neutrophil and total leukocyte counts
labs.quote: His complete blood count showed rising neutrophil and total leukocyte counts over time (Table 1).

labs.name: creatinine and liver enzymes
labs.quote: The patient’s creatinine levels and liver enzymes were progressively rising indicating both liver and renal insult (Table 2).

treatment.name: intravenous fluid resuscitation and proton pump inhibitor therapy
treatment.quote: On hospital admission, intravenous fluid resuscitation and proton pump inhibitor therapy were initiated.

treatment.name: admission to ICU with conservative management including intravenous dexamethasone
treatment.quote: the patient was subsequently admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) and was subjected to a conservative management approach, which included the administration of intravenous dexamethasone (Table 3).

treatment.name: oxygen supplementation via non-rebreathing mask
treatment.quote: To address the escalating respiratory demands, the patient was given oxygen supplementation through a non-rebreathing mask.

treatment.name: vitamin C and vitamin E
treatment.quote: The therapeutic regimen encompassed the continued administration of intravenous dexamethasone, supplemented by vitamin C and vitamin E (Table 3).

treatment.name: ceftriaxone
treatment.quote: Antibiotics (ceftriaxone) were given to address the increased neutrophilic counts.

treatment.name: intravenous cyclophosphamide
treatment.quote: To address the advancing disease, intravenous cyclophosphamide was added.

cases.outcome_quote: However, the patient left the medical facility against medical advice which resulted in an adverse outcome. Tragically, the patient passed away on the second day after he left the hospital.
cases.sequelae: UNVERIFIED (pulmonary injury ongoing at discharge from care)
cases.notes: Adolescent; suicidal vs accidental intent unclear - authors describe ingestion as accidental ('the accidental consumption of paraquat coincided with the influence of marijuana'). No quantitative lab values available in text (tables not rendered in source text).
